The '''2026 Westminster City Council election''' took place on 7 May 2026, as part of the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections]]. All 54 members of [[Westminster City Council]] were elected, with the Conservatives retaking control of the council from Labour. The election took place alongside [[2026 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]].

== History ==
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some of the powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police and fire.<ref>{{cite web |title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils |url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government |access-date=10 October 2021 |website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since formation, Westminster City Council was run by the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] until the [[2022 Westminster City Council election|2022 election]], which marked both the first ever [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] administration of Westminster and the first ever non-Conservative administration.

== Changes since 2022 ==
By elections in [[West End (Westminster ward)|West End]] ward in September 2024 and [[Vincent Square (ward)|Vincent Square]] ward in February 2025 both resulted in Conservative gains from Labour, reducing Labour's council group to 28 seats.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burford |first=Rachael |date=2025-02-28 |title=Labour loses by-election in prestigious Westminster ward as Reform sees surge |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/labour-byelection-defeat-westminster-vincent-square-tories-reform-b1213916.html |access-date=2025-11-19 |website=[[The Standard (London newspaper)|The Standard]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Baston |first=Lewis |date=2025-02-28 |title=Tory Westminster by-election gain may not mean Labour doom |url=https://www.onlondon.co.uk/lewis-baston-tory-westminster-by-election-gain-may-not-mean-labour-doom/ |access-date=2025-11-19 |website=OnLondon |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Two Conservative councillors, [[Laila Cunningham]] in [[Lancaster Gate (ward)|Lancaster Gate Ward]] and Alan Mendoza in [[Abbey Road (ward)|Abbey Road]] ward, defected to [[Reform UK]] in June 2025 and November 2025 respectively.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burford |first=Rachael |date=2025-11-19 |title=Another Tory on flagship council defects to Reform as Farage eyes gains in London |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/tory-westminster-council-defects-reform-nigel-farage-alan-mendoza-b1258768.html |access-date=2025-11-19 |website=[[The Standard (London newspaper)|The Standard]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Ward results ==
The following are the candidate-level results for the 7 May 2026 election.<ref name="sopn">{{cite web |title=Statement of Persons Nominated |url=https://www.westminster.gov.uk/sites/default/files/media/documents/westminster-city-council-elections-statement-of-persons-nominated.pdf |website=Westminster City Council |access-date=12 April 2026 |date=10 April 2026 |format=PDF}}</ref><ref name="westminster2026">{{cite web |title=Local elections 2026, results |url=https://www.westminster.gov.uk/about-council/democracy/elections-referendums-and-how-vote/local-elections-2026-results |website=Westminster City Council |access-date=9 May 2026 |date=8 May 2026}}</ref> Vote shares and the majority figures are calculated on ballot papers counted, and the change column compares each candidate to the same-rank candidate of their party in the [[2022 Westminster City Council election|2022 election]], which was held under the same ward boundaries. Candidates of parties that did not contest the ward in 2022, or that fielded fewer candidates than in 2026, are marked N/A. Sitting councillors seeking re-election in their existing ward are marked with an asterisk (*); councillors seeking re-election for a different ward are marked with a cross (†). Three sitting Conservative councillors had changed party affiliation between the 2022 and 2026 elections: Alan Mendoza (Abbey Road) and [[Laila Cunningham]] (Lancaster Gate, the latter not seeking re-election in 2026) defected to [[Reform UK]],<ref name="defections-tory-reform">{{cite news |last=Burford |first=Rachael |date=19 November 2025 |title=Another Tory on flagship council defects to Reform as Farage eyes gains in London |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/tory-westminster-council-defects-reform-nigel-farage-alan-mendoza-b1258768.html |work=The Standard |access-date=9 May 2026}}</ref> while West End councillor Paul Fisher, who had been elected for [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] in 2022, defected to the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] before the election.<ref name="fisher-defection">{{cite news |title=West End councillor Paul Fisher quits Labour to join Tories |url=https://www.westminsterextra.co.uk/article/west-end-councillor-paul-fisher-quits-to-labour-to-join-tories |work=Westminster Extra |access-date=9 May 2026}}</ref>
